objective: Reproduce the newly generated glowing cyan-violet spiral plasma-core reference in an interactive, genuinely volumetric 3D SiteForge renderer, using existing authorized tools and mandatory Synestra procedures.

reference.authority: owner selected latest conversation image as target
reference.description: Large translucent glowing sphere, white-blue compact nucleus, winding broad cyan and violet plasma ribbons inside a dark indigo volumetric field, thin lightning, no metal rings or UI.
reference.reference_availability: VISUAL_IN_CONVERSATION, not embedded or copied into public production

root_cause: R153 plotted mostly 2D noise/filaments at reconstructed front-surface normal; its GPU POINTS could not show coherent spiral ribbon volume sampled from back to front. Old preview zoom .49 desktop / .8 mobile also made the sphere too small relative to reference.
changes: Convert primary fragment pass to a genuine ray-marched sphere volume integrating 3D density and emission from the front hemisphere through back with depth attenuation/transmittance and single 3D noise sample per step.
Use logarithmic swirling cyan-violet streams, longitudinal narrow filaments and broad bands at several rotated depths; preserve 4 preset modes electrically, vortically and fusion-distinct.
Rotate the 3D sample coordinates in response to pointer tilt; per-pixel 3D depth bounds, silhouette transparency and a soft cyan-violet rim.
Independent white-blue nucleus compact 3D radius and high-power radiance, HDR-like optical response with no fixed photo plane.
One existing WebGL1 shader program and canvas still execute 3D volumetric quad plus shell, internal branching lightning, compact core and extra particle GPU passes; no new 3D server/Bridge/broker.
Adaptive 14 mobile / 22 desktop ray samples, mobile DPR max 1.5 and pixel budget 650000, desktop higher quality.
Enlarge scene preview from old desktop scale .49 to .92 and mobile .8 to 1.22, no new UI: preserve 16 existing controls.
Make spiral ribbons broader with cyan/violet alternating channels; reduce overbright random shell sprite speckles to 28% of prior emission.
Update R154 GPU regression tests and legacy test expectations while preserving rollback and original reference SVG.

build.initial_failure: Two tests still matched historical shader version R153 and obsolete vec3 plasma variable; no observed shader failure.

real_browser.runtime: Actual Chromium WebGL, touch mobile 390×844 or 410×520 viewport, running exact current GitHub branch source in isolated HTML fixture (no Access bypass)
real_browser.source_access_qualification: The live preview is Access-protected; browser tests used a temporary HTML fixture that inlined the checked-in JavaScript and removed CSP only in the isolated fixture, never from the deployed site.
real_browser.snapshot_review: A real Cloudflare Chromium jpeg snapshot was rendered and manually inspected in session; cyan-violet spiral structure and white compact center visible, but visibly simpler and more speckled than reference. Framing enlarged and dot shell attenuated after first snapshot.
real_browser.benchmark_caveat: Headless Chromium under a comparable ~850 ms probe submitted about 9 ray-marched frames versus about 20 historical R153 shader frames. This is a relative synthetic browser observation, NOT measured iPhone FPS; quality vs performance remains a known issue.
real_browser.full_frame_perceptual_similarity: NOT_VERIFIED; no established objective similarity score or human approval
